findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, oversized file)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError>. Use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| ...) or ? operator to propagate errors to the caller.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value or if parts has fewer than 2 elements
findings.failure_mode: a single malformed CSV line crashes the entire telemetry load, losing all previously parsed records
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to extract the two fields. Call parse() with map_err to return a typed ParseError. Handle the case where split_once returns None (missing delimiter).

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy cast from u32 to u16 — silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a telemetry reading of 70000 becomes 4464 with no warning, corrupting the data silently
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32)? or check range with .checked_into() and return a typed OverflowError if out of bounds.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for a two-field CSV line. Then parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked index accesses.
findings.failure_mode: a line with more or fewer commas produces an out-of-bounds panic on parts[1], and every line heap-allocates an intermediate Vec
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get (&str, Option<&str>) for the second field. Trim and parse each field directly without collecting into a Vec. Use .get() or match/split_once pattern matching for field access.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a hidden side-effect (stdout I/O) inside a data-loading function that should be pure computation
findings.failure_mode: side effects in the core/telemetry-loading path make the function non-deterministic, untestable, and produce interleaved output when called from tests or other I/O contexts
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing pipeline. If logging is needed, push it to the imperative shell layer (caller) after parsing completes, or pass a logging callback. The pure core should not write to stdout.

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked indexing into a Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: if the line is empty or has zero fields, index 0 panics with out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and match on the Some((first, rest)) pattern, or use parts.first().ok_or(Error::MissingName) for bounds-safe access.

findings.problem: parts[1] is unchecked indexing into a Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a line with only one field (no comma) produces parts with length 1, and parts[1] panics with out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') — the second field comes from the Option<&str> return value, eliminating the need for indexing entirely.

findings.problem: load_telemetys returns Vec<Record> directly instead of Result — all errors (I/O, parse, overflow, missing fields) are hidden behind panics
findings.failure_mode: the function signature promises success but can fail silently via panic at any line, making error handling impossible for callers
findings.fix: Change signature to pub fn load_telemetry(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, TelemetryError>. Define a sealed error enum covering IoError, ParseError, OverflowError, and MalformedLine.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists to measure telemetry parsing throughput
no profiler data exists to identify hot paths in the parsing pipeline
no allocation analysis exists — split+collect+Vec allocates per-line and should be measured
no second-ring test evidence (property-based, fuzz, or adversarial input testing)
no command evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
residual_risk: static review only — no commands run. The crate has 8 BLOCKER violations: three unwrap calls, one lossy as cast, three unchecked index accesses, hidden println side-effect, and a return type that hides all error paths. A reviewer with access to the crate and cargo tooling should run cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo test to confirm findings before passing any delivery gate.
